data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 Jan 2017 was GBP 180.1m and closed at GBP 322.1m at 31 Dec 2017. The report does not provide a single, explicit gross prioryear movement figure; it states that "In 2017 the surplus was GBP 38.5m," indicating overall favourable development on prior years. 2017 was dominated by large natural catastrophe activity (Harvey, Irma, Maria, California wildfires, Mexico earthquakes) which materially impacted the 2017 year of account but was largely mitigated by the reinsurance programme. Prior years (notably 2015 and 2016) included both a benign period (2015) and specific events (Hurricane Matthew, Alberta fires) that influenced reserving outcomes.
raw_causal_phrases: the worst year for catastrophes in the US for over a decade with Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, the wildfires in California and earthquakes in Mexico causing insured market losses of $135 billion the costliest year on record (source: Munich Re).
The impact of the catastrophe losses on Syndicate 1910 net of reinsurance recoveries added 18.16 percentage points to the combined ratio.
The 2015 Year of Account has performed well and has returned a return on stamp of 16.1% thanks to a benign period of losses

data.data_quality_notes: No explicit GROSS prior-year movement (aggregate for years prior to 2017) is printed in a single labelled 'movement in prior years' line. The report states a surplus of GBP 38.5m in 2017 (text) which implies favourable prioryear development but does not quantify the gross movement. A gross claims development triangle is present but table alignment in the parsed text is ambiguous; rather than risk miscomputing a gross PYD from a partially ambiguous triangle, prior_year_development_gbp_m is returned as null. If a gross PYD is required, it can be approximated from the claims development table but the scanned/parsed layout here required manual interpretation.
